content.title: Every Song & Duet Performed at The Voice: Battle of Champions Finale
content.text: The Top 4 Finalists on The Voice: Battle of Champions truly brought their best to the April 14 Finale episode, each performing twice in competition (one ballad and one up-tempo song) and once in a duet with their Coach, creating an unforgettable night of music.How to WatchWhile there could ultimately only be one winner of The Voice Season 29, the Finale proved that all of the Artists — Liv Ciara, Lucas West, Alexia Jayy, and Mikenley Brown — are bound to have a booming and thriving music career. And their Coaches — John Legend, Kelly Clarkson, and Adam Levine — couldn't have been prouder.By the end of the evening, there wasn't a dry eye in the house, especially as the audience was made up of The Voice super-fans and former Voice Artists who knew exactly how much hard work went into each performance and what being a Finalist meant to them. It was an especially poignant comeback for Ciara, who auditioned for Season 28 and received zero chair turns, then made it onto Team Kelly in Season 29, nearly went home after her Battle against Brown only to be saved by the Super Steal, and — spoiler! — would end in the night in second place.RELATED: Stream New Episodes of The Voice: Battle of Champions the Next Day on PeacockRead on to revisit all of the songs performed throughout The Voice: Battle of Champions Finale on Tuesday night. Liv Ciara took on Billie Eilish, Christina Aguilera, and RihannaSong #1: "The Greatest" by Billie EilishThe 16-year-old singer chose the "saddest song ever" for her ballad: "The Greatest" by Billie Eilish, which made her Coach so teary that Legend had to assure Clarkson, "We're human, we're allowed to have emotions."Song #2: "What a Girl Wants" by Christina AguileraCiara also delivered a fun rendition of former The Voice Coach Christina Aguilera's "What a Girl Wants," which convinced her Coach that she's "ready to go" with her music career.Coach Duet: "Stay" by RihannaAt the end of the episode, Ciara and Clarkson sang a beautiful duet of Rihanna's "Stay."RELATED: Kelly Clarkson Reveals What Happens at The Voice Rehearsals: "There's A Lot..."Lucas West performed songs by Foreigner, John Legend, and Elton John Song #1: "Cold As Ice" by ForeignerStepping out from behind the piano, West showed off his rocker side with a lively performance of Foreigner's "Cold As Ice," which his Coach said he "killed" on stage. Song #2: "Ordinary People" by John LegendWest then paid tribute to his Coach with John Legend's first hit, "Ordinary People." Back on the keys, by himself on stage, West impressed the Coaches with his "purity" behind his instrument and made Legend "feel something" as he performed. Coach Duet: "Don't Let The Sun Go Down On Me" by Elton John Finally, both piano men saluted the ultimate piano master, Elton John, with a soulful duet of "Don't Let The Sun Go Down On Me."RELATED: John Legend Reveals the Feedback He Gives His Voice Team: "I Always Tell Them..."Alexia Jayy covered anthems by Adele, Patti LaBelle, and Maroon 5Song #1: "Lady Marmalade" by Patti LaBelleContinuing her strategy of covering big, brassy belters, Jayy first sang Patti LaBelle's "Lady Marmalade," which literally made Clarkson scream in her seat. Legend then gushed, "I just see a star up there, you carry yourself like you’re supposed to be on the Grammys."Song #2: "One and Only" by AdeleFor her second song of the Finale, Jayy had all of the Coaches "weeping" with her stunning cover of Adele's "One and Only."Coach Duet: "Sunday Morning" by Maroon 5Finally, Jayy made her son's dream come true by singing a song by his favorite band, Maroon 5, when her Coach joined her on stage to sing a fun duet of "Sunday Morning."RELATED: Alexia Jayy's "Bold" Knockout on The Voice Sounded Like These R&B Legends "Had a Baby"Mikenley Brown sang hits by Ariana Grande, Olivia Dean, and Billie EilishSong #1: "Almost Is Never Enough" by Ariana GrandeBrown chose another former Voice Coach, Ariana Grande, for her ballad, singing "Almost Is Never Enough," which led her Coach to confess that she's been trying to sing like her in the shower. "Girl your voice is so good, it’s gorgeous," Clarkson said. Song #2: "Man I Need" by Olivia DeanLater on in the Finale, Brown sang Olivia Dean's wildly popular hit song "Man I Need," which Levine said perfectly showcased her unique "style" as a performer.Coach Duet: "What Was I Made For?" by Billie EilishFinally, Brown and Clarkson sang a stirring duet of Billie Eilish's award-winning hit "What Was I Made For?"RELATED: Mikenley Brown's "Ethereal" Blind Audition Mesmerized The Voice: "I Didn't Even Recognize..."Alexia Jayy!After yet another night of incredible performances, the in-studio audience of former Voice Artists and super fans voted Jayy as the winner of The Voice Season 29, with Liv Ciara in second place as this season's runner-up. Lucas West placed third and Mikenley Brown placed fourth. ​"I'd say I can't believe it, but I can," Jayy's Coach Adam Levine said after the voting results were revealed. ​​​"There's no one more deserving of this honor."How to watch The Voice: Battle of Champions Finale performances Want to relive all of the musical mastery that went down at The Voice: Battle of Champions Finale on April 14? You're in luck — the full episode is available to stream the next day on Peacock, along with the rest of Season 29.
